item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports investigating ID–text representations, but does not establish gains for the exact from-scratch BERT4Rec setting. [DenseRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18442v1) learns a projection between pretrained content embeddings and collaborative ID embeddings, reporting improvements over SASRec, particularly when histories contain unseen items. Its pretrained encoder and different experimental backbone limit direct applicability here. [Enhancing ID and Text Fusion via Alternative Training (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.ijcnlp-long.12.pdf) identifies a useful failure mode: naive joint fusion can underperform ID-only recommendation because IDs dominate optimization while text remains undertrained. Its independently optimized modality approach should not be imported into this single-model experiment.\n\nA compatible research hypothesis is one BERT4Rec network with randomly initialized token embeddings, a small pooled title/description encoder, and a learned projection or gate combining text with item IDs. Shared words could transfer interaction supervision across sparse items; this is an inference, not a verified result from the cited studies. Modest ID dropout could test whether preventing ID dominance improves the jointly trained representation. Preserve [BERT4Rec’s masked-item objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690): hide both the ID and associated text at masked positions, preventing target leakage, and predict from an appended mask during inference. Train every component together and retain one checkpoint per category. Evaluate the hypothesis against ID-only BERT4Rec using the fixed macro validation HR@10; the retrieved evidence does not justify assuming an improvement."}
